ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a schematic diagram of a closed circulation composed of four sides. The arrow on the bottom side ① goes from right to left, indicating flow westward; the arrow on the left side ② goes from bottom to top, indicating flow northward; the arrow on the top side ③ goes from left to right, indicating flow eastward; the arrow on the right side ④ goes from top to bottom, indicating flow southward. The four sections of ocean currents are connected end to end, and as a whole present a clockwise direction. Then reason: If this diagram represents ocean circulation, a clockwise ocean circulation corresponds to the Northern Hemisphere subtropical circulation. In the figure, ① flowing westward can correspond to the North Equatorial Warm Current in the low latitudes of the North Pacific, ② flowing northward can correspond to the Kuroshio on the western coast, ③ flowing eastward can correspond to the North Pacific Warm Current, and ④ flowing southward can correspond to the California Cold Current on the eastern coast. These ocean currents together form the North Pacific subtropical circulation, so it is most likely to appear in the middle and low latitudes of the North Pacific.

method.method_draft: 先描述图像：图示为四边闭合洋流，①向西、②向北、③向东、④向南，整体顺时针。再把四段方向分别对应到北太平洋副热带环流中的北赤道暖流、黑潮、北太平洋暖流和加利福尼亚寒流。由这些洋流共同构成的环流位置判断，答案为北太平洋的中低纬度。
